title: policy catalog guardrails and autoremediator
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: Customers in regulated industries need automated enforcement of data residency and retention rules across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Current enforcement is fragmented: retention controls live in several services, residency metadata is set at provisioning time, and audit evidence is manually collected. This leads to silent config drift, missed retention deletions, and long audit prep cycles.

Proposal: Build a Policy Catalog + Autoremediator service that treats compliance controls as declarative policy-as-code and provides: a) real-time drift detection against the catalog, b) a safe plan/apply remediation pipeline (simulate -> propose -> canary -> apply), and c) tamper-evident evidence bundles for auditors. The service will integrate with existing runtime control plane to read effective routing/replication/retention settings, call KMS for signing evidence bundles, and push remediation ops to orchestrators (hosted control plane or a private connector for VPC customers).

Key design points: 1) Policy Catalog: declarative YAML rules with versioning and semantic constraints (e.g., residency: eu-west-1; retention: 90d min). Policies stored in Git-backed repo with web UI and policy diff previews. 2) Drift Detector: periodic and event-driven collectors compute desired vs actual state, emit a change set, and assign a risk score. 3) Autoremediator: supports dry-run (simulate) and staged rollout. Remediations produce signed change requests and evidence artifacts. 4) Evidence Bundles: for each remediation or periodic scan, produce a signed bundle (metadata JSON, diffs, snapshots, operator approvals) encrypted with customer KMS and exportable as ZIP/JSON lines for audits. 5) Safety and approvals: integrate with RBAC/SAML to require human approval for high-risk remediations and support canary target sets. 6) Observability: per-policy telemetry in Console and alerting when automated remediations cross thresholds.

Non-goals: this ticket does not implement UI polish for the policy editor (just core API + basic web surface), nor the private connector binary packaging (that is a separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Policy Catalog API that accepts declarative YAML policies and returns policy IDs and diffs
Drift detector that produces a reconcile plan containing desired/actual diffs for residency and retention rules
Autoremediator execute plan flow supporting simulate -> propose -> apply with canary targets
Evidence bundles generated for every apply, signed with KMS-compatible key and exportable from Console
RBAC-enforced approval gate for high-risk remediations configurable per-customer
Automated tests covering reconciliation logic and a staging run against test fixtures
Telemetry emitted to Console: per-policy drift count, remediation success/failure, and time-to-remediate
tasks: Design policy schema and validation rules (residency, retention, allowlist/denylist)
Implement Git-backed catalog service + REST API and policy diff endpoint
Build collectors for effective runtime state (routing, replication, retention metadata)
Implement reconciliation engine that outputs a safe plan and risk score
Autoremediator planner: simulate vs apply modes and canary targeting
Evidence bundle generator with JSON snapshot, diffs, operator approvals, and KMS signing
Add RBAC hooks and approval workflow integration with Console
CI tests and end-to-end staging run using synthetic customer fixtures
Create initial Console pages for policy listing, pending remediations, and evidence export

2025-03-03 Priya Nair (PM): Requested that evidence bundles include operator IP and request correlation IDs to support audits. Also asked for export as NDJSON for SIEM ingestion.
2025-03-05 Engineering review: Concern about mutation windows when remediating retention in Dedicated — added canary target and scheduled off-peak enforcement by default.
